## Summary

The sprint's goal — fire the Tier-2 arm once and produce #307's adoption-decision material — was delivered: `docs/loop-engineering/tier2-firing.md` records `rounds_avoided = 0`, below both the measured (≈0.341) and modelled (≈0.739) break-even thresholds. Getting there took a mid-sprint pivot: period 1 (`T-1086`, its re-cut `T-1089`) stopped twice on the same "guard-weaker-than-prose" defect class recurring across three review rounds (Majors 2→4→6) despite two structurally different repairs, while QA passed every round. The operator's 2026-08-22 review-depth re-pricing (dev-scaffold check lines judged on computed values and real defects, not adversarial guard-completeness) unblocked period 2: `T-1090` (PR #337), `T-1087` (PR #338, 3 substantive rounds) and `T-1088` (PR #339, the firing itself, one round each gate) all closed clean. The R2 exit decision (parallelization downgraded to future, or R1 begins) is a planning decision this retro hands off rather than makes.

## Keep

- QA and cross-provider review both caught self-reported computed-value errors exactly where they should — `T-1090`'s QA round 1 failed on a self-contradicting `AC7(b)` count (board commit `72aad55`; independently confirmed corrected in `.shell-team/reviews/T-1090.md:19`), and `T-1088`'s Codex round 1 caught `.shell-team/provenance/T-1088.md`'s "77 named steps" against the correct, re-derived 76 (`.shell-team/reviews/T-1088.md:23,39`). Two independent catches of the same defect shape (a hand-counted tally versus a command-derived one) at two different gates in one sprint.
- When a reviewer agent's write access was mistakenly revived mid-task by a stale background-task notification and it wrote a commit onto the wrong branch of a shared checkout, it held its own write boundary — stopped, refused to self-correct via checkout/cherry-pick/reset, and reported to the coordinating session rather than acting unilaterally (`.shell-team/interventions/T-1087.md`, third entry). Recovery was verified twice over (cherry-picked copy plus reflog) before the branch was reset; zero work lost.
- The pre-commitment mechanism fired as designed, twice, in period 1: `T-1086` stopped at its own same-class-2 gate (commit `ea393b4`; `.shell-team/interventions/T-1086.md`) and `T-1089` stopped at same-class-3 (commit `6dc38c1`) rather than absorbing a fourth patch round on a class that two structurally different repairs (class-M re-freeze, class-B re-freeze) had already failed to close.
- The re-priced review scope produced fast, still-substantive closes in period 2: `T-1090` closed in one QA kickback plus one Codex round (APPROVE, zero findings — `.shell-team/reviews/T-1090.md`), and `T-1087`'s three rounds were all real substance (quote-fidelity drift, a merge-unreachability soundness gap, the X/Y disjoint-subset counterexample — `.shell-team/reviews/T-1087.md` rounds 1-2, board `T-1087` entry), never a guard-completeness Major reappearing under the new pricing.
- A live process trap was found, fixed, and written down for reuse rather than silently worked around: `T-1087` verified and documented the "double-backgrounding" hazard (a trailing shell `&` plus the harness's own `run_in_background: true` silently truncates tracked output) and a worktree-runs-corpus symlink fix, both appended to `.shell-team/test-recipe.md` (commit `c411a67`).

<!-- retro-section: problem -->
## Problem

- Period 1 spent two full tasks (`T-1086`, `T-1089` — 4 combined review rounds across both) on the same "guard-weaker-than-prose" defect class before an operator pivot changed what the review gate priced, with QA green every round while adversarial review kept defeating hand-written inline `- check:` lines (never the shipped `bin/` checkers themselves) — git commits `31041a8`/`0ff969b`/`d31dfb1`; `.shell-team/reviews/T-1089.md` rounds 1-3. The reviewer's own round-3 note named the shape directly: "a hand-written shell-script guard verifying a natural-language claim about a hand-written shell-script guard is recursively similar in shape to the original oracle-vs-unbounded-candidate-input problem this entire task exists to solve" (`.shell-team/reviews/T-1089.md:257`).
- Two structurally different remedies both failed to close the class: route (a) (full-population check-line sweep, class-M re-freeze) and route (b) (operator-ratified claim re-scope, class-B re-freeze) each produced new instances of the identical general pattern rather than closing it (`.shell-team/reviews/T-1089.md:155,245`; `.shell-team/interventions/T-1089.md`), matching the "an omission class is not closed by sweeping again" pattern `.shell-team/lessons.md` already names (lines 401-420) — recurring here one level up, on the guards themselves rather than on the guarded content.
- A stale background-task notification revived a reviewer agent's write access after its own verdict had already been processed and committed, and the agent wrote directly into a shared checkout that had since moved to a different task's branch, landing a stray commit on the wrong task's frozen-spec commit (`.shell-team/interventions/T-1087.md`, third entry). Recovery was clean, but the underlying race — notification staleness versus shared-checkout branch state — is not itself closed by that recovery.
- Codex CLI stalled at `turn.started` multiple times on large combined-diff prompts during the `T-1088` arm's gate rounds (`docs/loop-engineering/tier2-firing.md`, `## Limits`, "codex-invocation incidents": the winner's round-1 combined call stalled 3 times against a 9 s control-prompt baseline; the loser's round-1 call stalled twice, killed 143). Reviewers self-recovered by splitting scope, but the note discloses the resulting coverage as partial/empirical for one half rather than a completed automated pass.
- The arm's own comparator carries a disclosed gate-instrument-variance limit: the two candidates' round counts (`r_winner = r_loser = 3`) were not measured by an identical probe battery — one reviewer instance constructed a `/dev/zero` non-EOF-device probe the other never tried, plus an opposite-direction probe-hint asymmetry — so either count could plausibly have shifted by one, exactly the comparator's 0.5-round resolution (`docs/loop-engineering/tier2-firing.md`, `## Limits`).

<!-- retro-section: try -->
## Try

- Write the 2026-08-22 review-depth re-pricing into the standing scaffolding (e.g. a dev-scaffold spec-class boundary referenced from `agents/codex-reviewer.md` or a template block) rather than leaving it as a ruling each task must transcribe verbatim into its own `## Verdict scope` — three tasks this cycle (`T-1090`, `T-1087`, `T-1088`) each carried that transcription as its own byte-faithfulness obligation at freeze time. Owner: pm-spec / tech-lead, on the next task touching a dev-scaffold spec.
- Make "does defeating this check line require reopening the enumerated-case oracle itself, or is it bounded, closable work on the guard's own grammar" an explicit pre-commitment discriminator, checked before counting rounds toward a same-class stop — `T-1089`'s round-3 adversarial pass already did this classification informally and judged all five new findings "bounded" (`.shell-team/reviews/T-1089.md:239`), which is the judgment that should gate a same-class-N stop versus ordinary rework. Owner: pm-spec, at pre-commitment authoring time.
- After a QA round catches one self-reported computed tally as wrong, independently recount the same hand-off's other self-reported tallies before closing the round, not only the one flagged value — the pattern predicts more than one site per report, and `T-1088`'s independent "77 vs 76" catch two tasks later suggests this per-report scan is not yet standard practice. Owner: qa-verifier.
- Give Codex review invocations a pre-declared prompt-size threshold above which the call is pre-split into per-component scoped invocations, rather than discovering the stall after 1-3 timeouts — `docs/loop-engineering/tier2-firing.md`'s own disclosure (9 s control prompt vs. repeated `turn.started` stalls on the combined form) suggests the split-vs-combine decision is measurable in advance. Owner: codex-reviewer role / `bin/resolve-executor.sh` callers.
- Turn the ad hoc gate-instrument-variance disclosure `tier2-firing.md` invented (probe-battery asymmetry naming) into a reusable `## Limits` subsection template for any future multi-instance comparison, so a second Tier-2 firing does not re-derive the same disclosure shape from scratch. Owner: whoever authors the next tier2-firing note.

I did **not** open the raw Codex `-codex-*.jsonl`/`.txt` capture files (32 across this cycle) beyond grepping two of them for specific strings (`turn.started`, "77 named steps"); for everything else I relied on the board/review `.md` files' own attested re-derivations of those captures (e.g. QA's independent byte-for-byte arithmetic re-derivation, Codex's own independent re-verification passes) rather than the raw capture bytes. That is the one class of source I read only through a second-hand summary, not the primary artifact.

<!-- retro-section: lessons -->
## Lesson candidates

- `[common]` A dev-scaffold verification pipeline can accumulate an unbounded adversarial loop when the review gate treats "does an inline guard defend against every conceivable defeat" as a Major class on internal, non-shipped check lines — the guard is then reviewed by the same adversarial standard as the product surface it exists only to verify, and no number of patch rounds converges (source: `.shell-team/reviews/T-1089.md` rounds 1-3, the same class recurring 2→4→6 Majors across two structurally different repair routes, resolved only by an operator re-pricing decision). Firing condition: a spec's own inline `- check:` lines are drawing Major findings for hypothetical defeats rather than wrong computed values, conclusion direction, or a real instrument defect, for two consecutive rounds → before authorizing a third patch round, re-examine whether the review's Major bar for that spec class is priced at product-surface adversarial depth when the artifact is dev-only scaffolding.
- `[target-specific]` In this repo's stacked batch-GO cycle shape, a later task can be stacked on an **earlier task's tip even after that earlier task goes `BLOCKED` and returns to planning** — the chain does not rebase onto develop just because a link stopped (source: this cycle's board `- branch: … stacked on …` lines for `T-1090`/`T-1087`/`T-1088`, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` checks independently confirming `develop → T-1086(BLOCKED) → T-1089(BLOCKED) → T-1090 → T-1087 → T-1088`). Firing condition: a retro is invoked mid-sprint or before batch GO and the board shows any in-scope task `BLOCKED` and returned to planning → do not treat merge-commit history as the cycle window (it returns zero or foreign commits); reconstruct the window from each task's own `stacked on` line plus adjacent `git merge-base --is-ancestor` checks instead (adjacent to `.shell-team/lessons.md`'s existing 2026-08-11/2026-08-13 stacked-cycle entry — this extends it to the specific case where a chain link is a `BLOCKED`, unmerged predecessor rather than a merged one).
- `[common]` An agent's self-reported computed tally (a step count, a case count, a sweep total) errs at a rate that tracks how much of the number required actual counting versus a verbatim copy from a command's own output — this sprint reproduced the pattern twice, at two different gates, on two different tasks (`T-1090`'s QA-caught `AC7(b)` self-contradiction; `T-1088`'s Codex-caught "77 vs 76" named-steps count), consistent with an earlier operator-memory finding that engineer self-reports err proportionally to exposure. Firing condition: a hand-off report states a count or tally that required counting rather than transcribing verbatim from a command's own output → the reviewing gate independently recounts that specific value with its own command before accepting the report (adjacent to `.shell-team/lessons.md`'s existing "don't take an engineer's self-reported result at face value ahead of cross-provider review" entry, line 51 — this narrows that general caution to numeric tallies specifically).
- `[target-specific]` A background-task notification can arrive and resume an agent's write access after that agent's own verdict has already been processed and committed, and if the checkout is shared across tasks, the resumed agent may write onto whatever branch is currently checked out rather than the branch its own task belongs to (source: `.shell-team/interventions/T-1087.md`, third entry). The agent's own discipline — stop, do not self-correct via checkout/cherry-pick/reset, report to the coordinating session — is what kept the recovery lossless, and is the part worth preserving rather than the incident's specifics. Firing condition: a background review/QA agent is resumed by a stale completion notification after its task's board flag has already advanced past the state that notification was for → treat write access as revoked; verify the checkout's current branch matches the agent's own task before writing anything, and report rather than act if it does not match.
- `[target-specific]` Codex CLI invocations combining a large multi-file diff into one prompt are measurably more stall-prone (repeated `turn.started` hangs) than the same review split into scoped per-component calls, while a small control prompt completes quickly (source: `docs/loop-engineering/tier2-firing.md`, `## Limits`, "codex-invocation incidents" — 3 stalls on a combined prompt versus a 9 s control-prompt baseline). Firing condition: a Codex review call's prompt is built from more than roughly one component's worth of diff (a threshold this lesson does not itself set) → pre-split the call into per-component scoped invocations before attempting the combined form, rather than attempting-then-retrying after a stall.
